calibration_rulings.title: The pronouns of the class «جنہیں / انہیں / انہوں / جنہوں / تمہیں»: U+06C1, or U+06BE («جنھیں / انھیں …»)?
calibration_rulings.binds: No string today. b3, b5 and every later text where a pronoun of the four arises.
calibration_rulings.ruling: RE-WEIGHED IN ROUND 2: THE RULING STANDS, NARROWER. A, for the pronouns a text of this site can carry: «جنہیں», «انہیں», «انہوں», «جنہوں», and the forms built on them, are written with U+06C1. What carries the ruling, and is sound: the three outlets this reader reads that gave article text print them with a heh and never with U+06BE (the count does not tell U+06C1 from U+0647: clause (a) of the evidence), the Gulf's Urdu paper among them; the named dictionary heads all three of these words it was read for with U+06C1 (the fourth ruled form, «جنہوں», has no dictionary page behind it (three entry pages were read) and 1 press token on the three outlets against the broadcaster's 5); two blind readers passed the spelling in place; it is the provisional rule under which every page so far was written, and the spelling the stage checker and role file 05 are built for. B is not an error: it is the spelling of the reference site, of one broadcaster and, as far as is known, of the reformed orthography; it is not written on this site. TAKEN OUT OF THE RULING: the fifth pronoun of round 1's list, «تمہیں», with the other forms of the pronoun «تم». Round 1 ruled it with the class; the one reference read for it heads it with U+06BE, no outlet gave a token of it, and under the site's address rule (config: the honorific pronoun only) no text can carry it. It is not ruled either way; if a quoted text ever needs it, it is raised then with this evidence. Ruling P22a is untouched: U+06BE stays where it is a true aspirate. WHAT THIS BINDS: every /ur/ text, interface and pages alike, from round 2 of the line on. No approved string changes, because none carries a pronoun of the class, and no string of b4 does since round 2. Limits of the evidence, stated: three outlets against one, on one morning; one of the two named references unread; the committees unread. On record for the owner, one line: if he prefers the reformed spelling, B is a mechanical change over the four forms, none of which stands on the site today. ‖ THE EVIDENCE, as b4 round 2 measured it: ROUND 2: the entry is rewritten so that it stands alone and says only what was measured. WHERE IT WAS MET: round 1's text of uqair-mosque::summary carried «جنہیں» once, the first pronoun of the class in any Urdu text of the site; two blind readers read the pronoun in that field, the first in stage 5's text and the second in round 1's, and neither remarked on its spelling. Since round 2 that clause is worded with «جن کی» (change 0 of b4's round 2, made because two readers rejected the clause's verb, not for the spelling). So no string of b4, of b3 or of the applied site carries a pronoun of the class today: by the judge's script (b4/s7b-pre.mjs), the four forms and their U+06BE spellings occur 0 times in every Urdu value of the 58 attraction files (11 carry Urdu), in src/i18n/ui.ts, in tm.json and in b3's round-2 text. WHAT IS SOUND. (1) Press, by script on 2026-10-13 (b4/s7-p22-press.mjs, output s7-p22-press.out.txt): on the three outlets from which article text was fetched — urdunews.com (the Gulf's Urdu paper), express.pk, independenturdu.com — these pronouns are written with a heh and never with U+06BE: 12 and 0, 15 and 0, 18 and 0 tokens; on bbc.com/urdu with U+06BE and never with a heh: 0 and 44. (2) The reference dictionary the line's config names, entry pages read by script (b4/s7-p22-dict.mjs in round 1; b4/s7b-p22-refs.mjs in round 2, output s7b-p22-refs.out.txt): the headwords of rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-jinhen, meaning-of-inhen and meaning-of-unhon are written with U+06C1 (the page titles, code point by code point), and those pages carry the U+06C1 spelling 20, 32 and 19 times against 0, 3 and 3. (3) The reference site (stage 4): «جنھیں» 6654 pages against «جنہیں» 104, «انھیں» 29983 against «انہیں» 2273 — B by a wide margin, on a wiki whose spelling is normalised. (4) Two blind readers of this batch read «جنہیں» in place without a remark. WHAT WAS NOT SOUND IN ROUND 1's ENTRY AND IS WITHDRAWN FROM THE GROUNDS. (a) It said '12 with U+06C1': the script counts U+06C1 and U+0647 together (some outlets type the Arabic letter), so its counts say 'a heh and not U+06BE', not which heh. (b) It said 'five outlets of six': nawaiwaqt.com.pk (3 tokens) and dawnnews.tv (2) are too thin to count as outlets, and several of the 'pages' fetched from them and from jang.com.pk were style sheets, images and share links, not articles (the output lists the URLs); jang.com.pk and dunya.com.pk gave no text. The sample is one morning: three outlets with a heh, one with U+06BE, 89 tokens on those four. (c) Gathered in round 1 and not reported: the dictionary's SEARCH page for the U+06BE spelling of «انھیں» answered HTTP 200 and carries that spelling 29 times against 1 — a page that lists what matches its own query, so weak evidence, but it counts the other way. (d) It cited 'the repository's letterform guard' for a set of eleven consonants: the repository's tools/check-ur-text.mjs has no test of U+06BE at all. The set is in the round's stage checker (see the guard). (e) NEW IN ROUND 2, against the class as round 1 worded it: the same dictionary heads the fifth pronoun of the class with U+06BE (entry page meaning-of-tumhen, title code points 062A 064F 0645 06BE 06CC 06BA; 28 on the page against 3 with U+06C1). The dictionary does not spell the class one way. NOT READ, in either round: the Urdu Lughat (udb.gov.pk answered HTTP 500 or not at all, in both rounds on 2026-10-13), which is the other reference the config names; and any page of the orthography committees, whose recommendation is, as far as stage 4 and both judges know, B.
calibration_rulings.guard: WHAT GUARDS THE RULING TODAY. (1) Stage checker, this clause, read from this file by R/tools/lib/rulings.mjs on the judge rounds and finals of the attraction batches: none of «جنھیں», «انھیں», «انھوں», «جنھوں» occurs. (2) Stage checker, R/tools/lib/textcheck.mjs, line 48: U+06BE is a finding (code ASPIRATE) after any letter outside its set of eleven consonants (U+0628, U+067E, U+062A, U+0679, U+062C, U+0686, U+062F, U+0688, U+0691, U+06A9, U+06AF). That stops the four banned spellings in any stage file; it would also stop the unruled U+06BE spelling of the fifth pronoun, so the set is part of that question if it is ever raised. (3) THE BUILD DOES NOT TEST THIS LETTER. tools/check-ur-text.mjs in the repository has no rule on U+06BE (its forbidden letters are the eight Arabic letterforms), so a banned spelling in an applied file passes the build today, and only the round's stage checker would stop it on its way there. Whether the four banned forms become a build guard is LEFT TO THE COORDINATOR. For the proofreader, checklist item 1: a pronoun of the four is reported if it carries U+06BE.

calibration_rulings.title: The 'Site status' row of a mosque under restoration (uqair-mosque practical[0]; build check C29, clause d): its Urdu label and value.
calibration_rulings.binds: uqair-mosque::practical[0].label and ::practical[0].value. The label binds every later mosque page whose source carries the 'Site status' row; the value is this page's alone. b3: no such row.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. The label of the status row of a mosque under restoration is «مقام کی حالت»: it says what the English and the Arabic label say, in two words the round has approved, and is kept apart from khuzam's «موجودہ حالت», which renders another source label. The value on uqair-mosque is «بندرگاہ کے احاطے میں مرمت کا کام جاری ہے، اور ممکن ہے کہ اس کے کچھ حصے بند ہوں»: the subject is the source's (the port complex), the closure stays a possibility, the value ends without a stop (ruling P26), and it does not say whether the mosque itself can be entered. D is not taken: neither source row names the port. FOR THE COORDINATOR, byte for byte from this file: RESTORATION_LABEL.ur = «مقام کی حالت»; UNDER_RESTORATION for uqair-mosque.md, ur = «بندرگاہ کے احاطے میں مرمت کا کام جاری ہے، اور ممکن ہے کہ اس کے کچھ حصے بند ہوں»; and for RETIRED_IN of the same file the Urdu of the retired body sentence, which is the last sentence of the approved uqair-castle body: «اس مقام پر مرمت کا کام جاری ہے، اور ممکن ہے کہ اس کے کچھ حصے بند ہوں۔». ROUND 2: LABEL AND VALUE CONFIRMED, byte for byte as quoted above; neither moved in round 2, and the build script compares both with the text. One thing more for the coordinator on RETIRED_IN (the proof pass's finding 17, checked by the judge in tools/check-mosque-card.mjs): the five languages of that table hold only the first clause of the retired sentence ('The site is undergoing restoration work'). The matching Urdu clause is «اس مقام پر مرمت کا کام جاری ہے». An entry made of the whole sentence would not catch that clause written alone; the clause is what the other five entries correspond to. His to choose.
calibration_rulings.guard: Build check C29, clause (d), once its two Urdu entries are filled from this file. For the proofreader, not machine-read: on uqair-mosque the fixed visiting string is absent, the card promises no open visit, and neither summary nor body says that works are under way.

calibration_rulings.title: The title of uqair-mosque, where the pattern of item N43-title-with-a-translated-direction gives two possessives in a row.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «العقیر کی بندرگاہ کی مسجد», one pattern with the two tahimiyah titles (item N43-title-with-a-translated-direction) and the port in the form the approved pages write. The body does not call the mosque by its title, as the source does not. Round 1 opened it with a description built on the title's words and the source's 'historic'; the second reader found that sentence circular, the port standing in its subject and again in its place. Since round 2 the body opens «یہ تاریخی مسجد خلیج کے ساحل پر، الاحساء کے مشرق میں، العقیر کی تاریخی بندرگاہ کے احاطے میں واقع ہے۔»: the mosque by a demonstrative and the source's 'historic', the port named once, in the place. C stays on record as the fallback if a later reader trips on the two possessives.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the title begins with the place name as its termbase key writes it and carries no Arabic generic.

calibration_rulings.title: abubakr-mosque body: whose house and schools — the Arabic's person or the English's family?
calibration_rulings.binds: abubakr-mosque::body. Any later sentence where the two sources name different owners of one thing.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. Where the English and the Arabic of a field differ on whose a thing is, the Urdu states the Arabic's fact: «شیخ ابو بکر کے گھر اور ان کے دینی مدارس کے قریب». The kunya stands in its citation form because it stands alone as a person's name; inside the page's title, after the word for 'son of', the genitive stays (the two batches' agreed forms, SHARED-10). The first reader's question is the source's defect and is logged for the owner; nothing is added to say who the sheikh is, and the house is not tied to the ribat of b3's page, which no source does. B is on record as the owner's option if the English is the one he keeps.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the kunya is in the citation form only where it stands alone.

calibration_rulings.title: 'A heritage mosque', 'one of Al-Ahsa's oldest heritage mosques': Urdu has no adjective from the noun for heritage.
calibration_rulings.binds: abubakr-mosque::summary (changed in round 1 and again in round 2), abubakr-mosque::body (unchanged). Every later 'heritage' said of a building. b3: its «الاحساء کے ورثے کی پہچان» (qubba-mosque) does not say heritage of a building, so the guard does not reach it; it is neither of the two frames and is not touched.
calibration_rulings.ruling: E. 'Heritage' of a building is said with the noun, never with the word for 'historic', which would make one Urdu word of the two the Arabic keeps apart. As a statement about one building the noun takes its owner: «… ایک مسجد، جو الاحساء کے ورثے کا حصہ ہے». In a superlative frame, the possessive approved on qasr-ibrahim: «الاحساء کے ورثے کی قدیم ترین مساجد میں سے ایک». D is withdrawn: without an owner the noun was empty to the reader who met it and left the reading of an inheritance open. 'Of Al-Ahsa' in the summary is a word of the page's own body, not of the summary's source: no fact enters the page, since both sources of the body say whose heritage, and it is counted under accuracy as a word from another field. It is taken because the Urdu noun needs an owner in order to mean heritage at all; item N61-district-generic-in-a-summary, which keeps a district's class word out of a summary whose sources lack it, is not moved by this. The owner is one that a source of the same page names (here the body's 'of Al-Ahsa'); it is counted each time as a word from another field; and where no field of the page names an owner, the statement is raised, not completed. The clause «ورثے میں شمار ہوتی ہے» stays withdrawn for a building. B is refused under the role file (a distinction the Arabic makes) although both readers ask for it; it stays on record for the owner as the wording that reads most easily. THE BODY'S FRAME HAS FAILED ITS TEST: round 1 named the next blind reader as its test, and he, like the first, hears it as translated. It is kept all the same, because every remedy either reader wrote is B. Nothing inside this ruling is left to try in the body; the cost is charged under nativeness, and the cure — B, or a source that says what 'heritage' means here — is the owner's.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: where the source says 'heritage' of a building the Urdu carries the noun for heritage with its owner, in one of the two frames above. The owner is one that a source of the same page names; it is counted each time as a word from another field; and where no field of the page names an owner, the statement is raised, not completed.

calibration_rulings.title: 'Grammar' as a subject taught beside fiqh.
calibration_rulings.binds: hubaish::body, abubakr-mosque::body. Every later list of subjects taught in a mosque or a school of religious learning.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. Beside fiqh, exegesis or hadith, grammar as a subject of study is «نحو», bare. B beside fiqh reads as 'rules'; C adds morphology and D adds 'Arabic', neither of which the source names. No gloss is added: neither source glosses the word.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the word stands only beside another subject of study, never alone in a sentence where it could be read as its homograph.

calibration_rulings.title: On a mosque page, visitors who are not the mosque's: 'visitors to the area', 'the story the old port tells its visitors'.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, as an application of the last sentence of ruling N29: on a mosque page, visitors of a district, a port or any place other than the mosque take neither ruled noun; they are said with the phrase «آنے والوں», tied to their place — «علاقے میں آنے والوں کے لیے», «اپنے ہاں آنے والوں کو». The phrase does not stand bare straight after the noun of the place they come to, where it was read as one phrase with it.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the mosque word for visitors stands in this batch in the mosque rows only (five cells).

calibration_rulings.title: May a summary carry the district generic before a district's name when its own source names the district bare?
calibration_rulings.binds: hubaish::summary, umzurainiq::summary. Every later summary that names a district.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. The fence is read field by field: a summary carries the district generic where the English or the Arabic of that summary carries it, and stands bare where neither does. Of the two readers who met the bare name, the first did not stumble on it for want of the generic and the second did, as a minor remark. The fence stands as stage 4 applied it: the lack is in both summaries of the source (logged), and half of his doubt, whether the direction belongs to the name, is not cured by the generic, as the body shows; whether a class word set before a name is form in the sense of ruling P23 is not settled here and need not be. B is on record as the owner's option, one line: «محلہ جنوبی الرفعہ میں تیرہویں صدی ہجری کی ایک مسجد، …»; the defect of the source (a place named with nothing to say what it is) is logged either way.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: no generic stands in a summary whose two sources have none.

calibration_rulings.title: The Eastern Province: the name said in Urdu, or the Arabic name with its article (ruling P1 read to the letter)?
calibration_rulings.binds: umzurainiq::body. Every later page that names the province.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. The province is «مشرقی صوبہ», inflected like any phrase («مشرقی صوبے کی مساجد»): an Urdu form in settled use for this province, which is the exception ruling P1 itself makes, and as a name said in Urdu words it has no article to keep — the case of the approved «جزیرہ نما عرب». The country is not named beside it where the page does not name it.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the province is written in these two Urdu words, in the direct or the oblique case, and the transliterated Arabic name is not written.

calibration_rulings.title: A district whose English name translates a direction and keeps the rest ('South Al-Rifaa').
calibration_rulings.binds: hubaish: summary, body, area. Every later district or village whose English name translates a direction.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: the Urdu translates what the English translates and keeps the name with its article (ruling P1) — «جنوبی الرفعہ», with the generic before the whole, «محلہ جنوبی الرفعہ». B's adjective carries an article of agreement and a feminine ending that an Urdu reader takes for an opaque word; C drops the article against P1 and goes to the entry for search. The first reader's doubt is the cost of the pattern and is recorded in the entry.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the direction is the Urdu adjective and stands before the name; the generic, where the field's source has one, stands before both.

calibration_rulings.title: The rider of ruling N14 (the page's name does not stand directly against another proper name in the opening sentence), which the ruling words for the fort pages: does it hold for a mosque page?
calibration_rulings.binds: hubaish::body, abubakr-mosque::body (the first sentence of each). b3: nothing moves — jalaniyah and bubakr-ribat open with the place, dibs has an adjective and qubba-mosque a bracket between the two names. Every later page.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: CONFIRMED. The rider is not a rule about forts: on any attraction page, where the opening sentence would set the page's own name directly against another proper name, either the place comes first or a comma follows the name; the judge of the page chooses. On hubaish and abubakr-mosque the comma stands, as on khuzam and muhairis. It is not owed where a common noun, an adjective or a bracket already stands between the two names — umzurainiq («مسجد ام زرینیق محلہ العویمریہ میں واقع ہے») and, in b3, dibs and qubba-mosque — and it is not owed where the place comes first. SCOPE (round 2): 'another proper name' is a name a reader can run together with the page's name — of a town, a quarter, a village, a person, a family or a building. A common noun that serves as a name and is written bare like any noun («خلیج», ruling P5) is not such a name: «قلعہ العقیر خلیج کے ساحل پر، …» on the applied uqair-castle page is neither changed nor failed by this rule, and no page of round 1 is. uqair-mosque's opening carries no page name at all since round 2 («یہ تاریخی مسجد خلیج کے ساحل پر، …»).
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: in the opening sentence of a body the page's title is never followed directly by the name of a town, a quarter, a village, a person, a family or a building. A common noun used as a name («خلیج») is not such a name. A check written from this passes every applied page as it stands, uqair-castle included. Two things such a check takes from the ruling: a generic that stands before the next name («محلہ العویمریہ») is the common noun between and not part of that name; and the rule is about the page's own title only: a place that is not the page, set against another name with only its generic between (the village in the openings of the two tahimiyah pages), is outside it.

calibration_rulings.title: The order of an area line whose source names no larger place as a bare name ('Al-Battaliyah village — northeast of Hofuf', 'Al-Koot district — central Hofuf').
calibration_rulings.binds: jalaniyah::area, unchanged. BINDS b4: hubaish «محلہ جنوبی الرفعہ، ہفوف کے وسط میں», umzurainiq «محلہ العویمریہ، ہفوف کے وسط میں» and uqair-mosque's area line keep the source's order as they stand. Round 1's six lines (al-uqair, jawatha-mosque, ameeriah, khuzam, baiah, uqair-castle) stand unchanged. Every later area line of the pattern. ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. Where the source's area line names no larger place as a bare name — it gives a village, a quarter or a port and then where that lies by a direction or a part of the town — the Urdu keeps the source's order: the place with its generic, then «،», then the position, which ends in a postposition: «البطالیہ گاؤں، ہفوف کے شمال مشرق میں», «محلہ الکوت، ہفوف کے وسط میں». Ruling P20 is untouched and holds wherever the source names a larger place as a bare name: that place leads («ہفوف، محلہ الکوت»; «الاحساء، مشرقی دیہات میں التہیمیہ گاؤں»). The two orders are therefore two cases of one rule — what the source gives as a bare larger name leads, and what it gives as a position follows — and no line of round 1 moves. Cost, stated: the same quarter can still stand quarter-first on one page and town-first on another where its sources word the line differently; that is logged with the sources' defects and is the owner's to even out in the source. On record for him, one line: B for every such line («ہفوف کے شمال مشرق میں، البطالیہ گاؤں»), which would move ten lines on applied pages. ‖ b4, ROUND 1: adopted as b3's judge ruled it; nothing moves. hubaish::area and umzurainiq::area keep the source's order and end in a postposition; uqair-mosque::area is the approved line of uqair-castle from the translation memory, which also ends in one; tahimiyah-e and abubakr-mosque lead with the larger bare place (ruling P20). b4's first reader read the five rows and remarked, as a minor item, that the row is built four different ways and that he had to re-orient each time (observation 7): the two cases of this rule over four wordings of the sources, logged with the sources' defects as this entry says. The checker's three notes of ruling P20 on b4 are these three lines and are expected. b4, ROUND 2: unchanged. The second reader of b4 (his item 47, minor) notes that abubakr-mosque's row puts the town first where hubaish and umzurainiq put the quarter first: the two cases of this rule over the sources' wordings, logged as before. The checker's three notes of ruling P20 are still these three lines.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker: its note of ruling P20 on an area line of this pattern is expected and is not a finding. For the proofreader, not machine-read: an area line that does not open with a bare larger place has a source that names none, and ends in a postposition, never in a bare place name after the comma.

calibration_rulings.title: A Hijri year or century whose Gregorian equivalent the source marks as approximate ('1280 AH (around 1863 CE)', 'the fifth century AH (around the eleventh century CE)').
calibration_rulings.binds: jalaniyah::body (the century), bubakr-ribat::body (two years). BINDS b4, unchanged: hubaish body «تیرہویں صدی ہجری (تقریباً انیسویں صدی عیسوی)». Every later page with such a pair. ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. Where the source gives a Hijri year or century and marks its Gregorian equivalent as approximate, the form is ruling N12's (or N11's) with the one word «تقریباً» inside the round bracket, before the Gregorian figure or ordinal: «1280 ہجری (تقریباً 1863 عیسوی)», «1430 ہجری (تقریباً 2009 عیسوی)», «پانچویں صدی ہجری (تقریباً گیارہویں صدی عیسوی)». The word stands only where the source has it and only on the side the source puts it: where the source's 'around' covers the Hijri date itself it stands before the pair, as on jabri-mosque («تقریباً 850 ہجری (1446 عیسوی)»). Nothing is converted, computed or evened out between pages: 1430 AH is «(2009 عیسوی)» on jalaniyah and «(تقریباً 2009 عیسوی)» on bubakr-ribat because their sources say so. ‖ b4, ROUND 1: adopted; the bracket of hubaish is unchanged. Since b4's round 1 the pair is followed by another verb, «تیرہویں صدی ہجری (تقریباً انیسویں صدی عیسوی) میں تعمیر ہوئی» (change 3 of b4's round 1, counted from 0), the frame of jalaniyah. b4's first reader read the pair twice (observations 9 and 22) and did not stumble on its form. b4, ROUND 2: unchanged. The second reader read the pair without a stumble on its form; his items 13 and 45 are on the sources' unevenness.
calibration_rulings.guard: The machine-read clauses of rulings N11 and N12 hold as they are (the stage checker passes this form under both). For the proofreader, not machine-read: the word for 'around' stands inside the bracket only where the source marks the Gregorian side as approximate, and is the round's one word for it.

calibration_rulings.title: A byname the source itself quotes and the English translates ('the village of forty mosques'): marks, gloss, «نامی»?
calibration_rulings.binds: tahimiyah-s::body. BINDS b4, as SHARED-05 has it: tahimiyah-e body carries the same clause word for word after its own opening words («خود یہ گاؤں»); its summary, whose English has a count and no byname, keeps «چالیس مساجد» without marks. ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, as a fourth place for quotation marks beside the three of ruling N16, point 5: a byname that the source itself sets in quotation marks and the English translates is written translated, inside U+201C and U+201D, with no gloss and no «نامی» (it is not a P3b name: nothing of it is Arabic). Its plural is the page's own («مساجد»). The shared clause, from its first word to its stop: «کبھی “چالیس مساجد کا گاؤں” کے نام سے مشہور تھا، اور ان مساجد میں سے اب تقریباً گیارہ ہی باقی ہیں۔» — 'only' is the particle and 'around' the round's one word, both the source's; that the two pull against each other (observation 47) is the source's sentence. ‖ b4, ROUND 1: adopted; tahimiyah-e body carries the shared clause after its own opening words, equal to b3's by script, and its summary keeps the count without marks. b4's first reader read the byname in its marks without a remark; what he noticed in the clause is the approximate word before a small count (observation 8), which is the source's. b4, ROUND 2: unchanged. The second reader read the byname in its marks without a remark; his item 12 is again the approximate word before a small count, the source's.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the byname stands inside its quotation marks at every mention, translated, with no bracket after it.

calibration_rulings.title: An Hours value that gives no clock time ('Open to visitors during daylight hours', Arabic 'available for visiting throughout the daylight hours').
calibration_rulings.binds: tahimiyah-s::practical[1].value. BINDS b4, as SHARED-04 has it: tahimiyah-e practical[1].value is this string byte for byte. The label is the approved «اوقات». ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: B, one string on both pages: «دن بھر زائرین کے لیے کھلی رہتی ہے». Where the two sources differ in strength the Arabic is followed ('throughout the daylight hours'), and that is counted under accuracy against the English's 'during'. No clock time is supplied, nothing is tied to prayer times, and the row is carried into no other field. That an Hours row stands on a mosque page beside the owner's fixed row, and what the owner's pending question would make of it, is logged for him; neither wording answers it. ‖ b4, ROUND 1: adopted; tahimiyah-e practical[1].value equals b3's string by script. b4's first reader (observation 19, minor): the row repeats the row above it, and the value is 'at least something to plan with, though it does not say from when to when' — the source's; no fault in the wording. b4, ROUND 2: unchanged. The second reader (item 16, moderate): the value leaves him unsure about the sunset and night prayers, and the page does not say whether prayers are held today — the source's; no fault in the wording.
calibration_rulings.guard: The two values are equal by script. For the proofreader, not machine-read: the value names no hour and ends without a stop.

calibration_rulings.title: A mosque with more than one prayer niche and with arches named in the same breath: ruling N34 marks the niche by the singular, which cannot hold here.
calibration_rulings.binds: jalaniyah::body. b4: its pages with arches (hubaish, umzurainiq) name no niche in the plural beside them and are not touched; the rule binds b4 only if such a sentence arises.
calibration_rulings.ruling: E. Round 1 ruled B and named the next blind reader as its test; B failed it and is withdrawn. On a page where niches in the plural and arches both stand, they do not share a sentence, and the arches are said first, among the materials and the roof and before any niche has been named: «ستونوں کی قطاروں پر نوک دار محرابیں ٹکی ہیں۔» Then the niches, with the wall and their number: «قبلے کی دیوار میں دو محرابیں اس مسجد کو منفرد بناتی ہیں۔» No word changes and none is added; the order of two statements of one source sentence is turned, which is form (ruling P23). D is not taken: ruling N34 keeps one word for the arch and a batch judge does not reopen it. C drops the source's noun. The cost of E is on record: one word still names two things in neighbouring sentences, and E has been read by no one; the next blind reader is its test. IF HE STUMBLES TOO, nothing inside ruling N34 is left to try: the text is then locked with E or B, whichever that round's judge finds the less harmful, and the cure both readers of this batch wrote, D, goes to whoever may reopen N34 — its mark for the arch (the plural) fails on a page whose niches are plural. ‖ b4, ROUND 1: nothing moves; neither page of b4 with arches names a niche. RECORDED for whoever may reopen ruling N34: b4's first reader (observation 24, moderate) pictured several prayer niches in a veranda at «گول محرابوں والا برآمدہ» (hubaish) before he worked out that arches are meant, and on umzurainiq cannot tell which is meant in «دیواروں، کھڑکیوں اور محرابوں پر گچ کے نقش و نگار». The plural, which is the mark ruling N34 gives the arch on a mosque page, was in place both times. He is the third reader of this round to take the plural for niches on a mosque page, and the first to do so on pages that name no niche at all: b3's round 2 records that the mark fails where the niches are plural; here it failed where there are none. A batch judge does not reopen N34, and the cost is charged under nativeness on both pages. b3's round 2 turned the order of its two sentences (candidate E); that moves nothing in b4. b4, ROUND 2: nothing moves. The second reader of b4 (item 26, minor) also took the arches of hubaish for prayer niches 'for a moment' and names umzurainiq's plural with it: the fourth reader of the round, and the second on pages that name no niche. Recorded as before for whoever may reopen ruling N34. ‖ AFTER THE LAST BLIND READ (b3/stages/06-blind-reader.on-r2.md, item 12, moderate; no judge round followed it): the reader of E stumbled too. He took the second sentence for two of the arches, read it twice, and wrote the word of candidate D for the first sentence. The final text carries E; D goes to whoever may reopen ruling N34.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: on jalaniyah the sentence of the arches stands before the sentence of the two niches, and the two are two sentences.

calibration_rulings.title: The Urdu title where title_en keeps only the place name and translates the rest ('Al-Tahimiyah West Mosque').
calibration_rulings.binds: tahimiyah-s::title. BINDS b4, as SHARED-02 has it: tahimiyah-e «التہیمیہ کی مشرقی مسجد»; uqair-mosque's title is built the same way. ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, one pattern for a title whose English translates everything but the place name: the place name as its key, the Urdu possessive, then the translated words in Urdu order — «التہیمیہ کی مغربی مسجد», «التہیمیہ کی مشرقی مسجد». The note ruling N14 added to the title rule (the Arabic generic first) is for names whose generic the English keeps, and is not touched. ‖ b4, ROUND 1: adopted; tahimiyah-e's title and its second name on the same pattern stand, and uqair-mosque's title is ruled under b4's item N56-title-with-two-possessives. The cost, on b4's first reader (observations 12 and 14): the title reads to him as a description, 'the eastern mosque of the village', not as what the mosque is called; and with the second name of abubakr-mosque, which its source translates the same way, he wondered whether two pages were about one mosque. The names are the sources'. b4, ROUND 2: unchanged. The second reader (item 14, moderate) says both things again: on tahimiyah-e he cannot tell whether «مشرقی مسجد» is the mosque's name or 'the eastern one', and with the second name of abubakr-mosque he went back to check that they are two places. Two readers of two: the stated cost, charged under fit on tahimiyah-e.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: such a title begins with the place name as its termbase key writes it, and carries no Arabic adjective with an article.

calibration_rulings.title: The Royal Commission for Jubail and Yanbu: the Urdu adjective for 'royal', or the press's loan?
calibration_rulings.binds: jalaniyah::body. BINDS b4, as SHARED-08 has it: uqair-mosque body writes the same key in the same oblique form. ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. The body is «الجبیل اور ینبع کا شاہی کمیشن»: the Urdu adjective for 'royal', the loan ruling N18 admits for a body called a commission, the two cities with the Urdu possessive; no quotation marks, and it inflects like any phrase (ruling N16, point 4) — in a sentence «الجبیل اور ینبع کے شاہی کمیشن نے». The press form goes to the entry for search and is not written. The entry stays pending for one reason only: nothing in Urdu attests this wording for this body. ‖ b4, ROUND 1: adopted; uqair-mosque body carries the name in the same oblique form, unchanged. RECORDED: b4's first reader (observation 41) 'could not tell at once that these are two place names', nor why a commission from elsewhere appears — one reader of the round's three so far; the second half is the source's. The entry stays pending for the reason this ruling gives. b4, ROUND 2: unchanged. The second reader (item 36, moderate) stopped on the name too — 'one commission or two, and why would a body for two other cities be repairing a mosque here'. Two readers of b4's two; the second half is the source's. The entry stays pending.
calibration_rulings.guard: Proofreader, checklist item 9: «کمیشن» stands here in the name of a body (ruling N18). Not machine-read: the name carries no quotation marks.

calibration_rulings.title: The sentence 'in 2017 it was listed among Al-Ahsa's officially registered historic mosques' (jalaniyah here, tahimiyah-e in b4): SHARED-12 of stage 4, changed by round 1 of b3's stage 7.
calibration_rulings.binds: jalaniyah::body. BINDS b4: tahimiyah-e body changes its sentence to exactly «2017 میں یہ الاحساء کی تاریخی مساجد کی سرکاری فہرست میں شامل ہوئی۔» — the same string in both batches from its first figure to its stop. Every later page that names the register. ROUND 2: unchanged — the same exact string for both batches; b4's text carries it since b4's round 1 (tahimiyah-e body).
calibration_rulings.ruling: B. One Urdu name for the one register on every page: «الاحساء کی تاریخی مساجد کی سرکاری فہرست». The sentence with a year is «2017 میں یہ الاحساء کی تاریخی مساجد کی سرکاری فہرست میں شامل ہوئی۔»; the sentence without one stays «… الاحساء کی تاریخی مساجد کی سرکاری فہرست میں درج ہیں» (tahimiyah-s). The year stays bare (ruling N12). It is a change of form under ruling P23 — the year, the list, its being official and the mosques being historic all stand — and it is counted under accuracy; A stays on record as the literal wording for the owner. SHARED-12 as stage 4 worded it is withdrawn. ‖ b4, ROUND 1: ADOPTED IN THE TEXT. tahimiyah-e body now carries exactly this sentence (change 1 of b4's round 1, counted from 0), copied by script from b3's jalaniyah body and compared: equal from the figure to the stop. b4's first reader had read stage 4's wording as a circle too (observation 17). The guard holds on b4's text. NUMBERING: in this file, as in b3's, the ids N46, N47 and N48 mean only what b3's judge ruled; the nine items b4's stage 4 had numbered N46 to N54 are N55 to N63 here. b4, ROUND 2: unchanged; the second reader of b4 read the sentence without a remark.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker: the string «جو سرکاری طور پر درج ہیں» does not occur. For the proofreader, not machine-read: the two sentences of jalaniyah and tahimiyah-e are equal by script.

open_items.title: A quoted Arabic word that is letter for letter an Urdu word («حسی», the singular of the name, reads as the adjective 'sensory'): how is the reader told what he is looking at?
open_items.provisional: Not settled: stays open. C is withdrawn — tried, read, no cure, and a word neither source carries; the conditions under which round 2 let it in (P23: the repaired text passes a blind read) were not met. The text stands in the wording of round 1, «لفظ “الاحساء”، “حسی” کی جمع ہے، یعنی …»: the order the first reader asked for and the second read without remark on the order. The homograph remains and is charged under fit. B, the remedy three readers ask for and the form the Arabic source itself uses, is barred by the P8 build guard (U+0650) and by ruling P17 as they stand, and a judge does not reopen a ruling. Recorded for whoever may: the build guard already exempts a termbase key that carries the sign (tools/check-ur-text.mjs, the registered-key exemption of P8), so the vocalised word would need an entry whose key carries the kasra and the sukun, the stage checker to honour the same exemption for a key the chain proposes, and the two signs in the Nastaliq subset.
open_items.first_bites: the home page as it stands; any later sentence that quotes an Arabic word which unvocalised spells an Urdu word (the etymology of a name, a dish, a craft term)
